8:

Stat. §14-10-113(1)(d)* (`library/columbia_equitable_distribution.md`). So the proposal is a **starting point, not a fair endpoint**.

Stat. §14-10-113(1)(d)*) — his lawyer's "exactly 50/50" line is the part of the math the statute says *not* to ignore.
25: - **"The biggest asset" is the most discounted one.** On paper: house $700,000 equity; his 401(k) $400,000; brokerage $300,000. 74: - **Option C fits the constraint precisely: it requires no refinance from you at all.** He stays on title *and* on the existing loan as co-obligor while you occupy under the decree, so no new underwriting happens. The exit trigger must be the **sale** (both names on the deed → both $250,000 exclusions), *not* your refinance. If instead you want to stay past the trigger date, the only financing exit is *his* refinance/buyout — treat that as a negotiated fallback term, not the plan.
75: - **Option B (sell now) is the fallback** if he refuses to stay on title/loan. Given the confirmed refinance constraint, the real choice is C-or-B — there is no safe "keep it alone" path.
76: - Caveat: Option C's feasibility depends on **his cooperation** (unresolved — §10). Expect him to demand indemnity, escrow, insurance and life-disability protection securing the loan; price those, don't fight the concept.

80: ## 4. Alternatives with numbers (same as `division.json`)
81: 
82: | Option | Wife after tax | Husband after tax | Instruments |
83: |---|---:|---:|---|
84: | Proposal kept, cash equalized (+$22,976 to you: cash 73/27) | $635,984 | $635,984 | cash transfer; no QDRO needed |
85: | Sell house now; everything else 50/50 (incl. QDRO $200,000) | $661,707 | $661,707 | sale; **QDRO**; equal splits |
86: | **Stay 6 years, deferred joint sale, both stay on title; everything else 50/50** | **$661,707** | **$661,707** | deferred sale + §121(d)(3) preservation; **QDRO $200,000**; indemnity |
87: 
88: Build-up for the 661,707 options: half of house net $297,227 + half 401(k) after tax $152,000 + half brokerage after tax $142,480 + half cash $50,000 + your car $20,000. **The recommended option leaves you ~$48,699 ahead of the proposal** and keeps the kids in the house.
89: 
90: ## 5. Instruments you need (and what a QDRO is)
91: 
92: - **QDRO ("qualified domestic relations order") — you need one if any part of his 401(k) comes to you.** A 401(k) division *must* be done by a QDRO; without one, a payout to you is **taxed to him** and, if he's under 59½, hit with a **10% penalty** — and you get nothing taxed-to-you basis. *26 U.S.C. §414(p); ERISA §206(d)(3)* (`library/qdro_72t.md`). Under a QDRO, your share is taxed to **you**, the 10% early-withdrawal penalty does **not** apply to QDRO distributions to you (*§72(t)(2)(C)* — a useful safety valve if you need cash before 59½), and you can roll it into an IRA. Get the QDRO entered with (not after) the decree.
93: - **Deed / title language for the house** that preserves the joint §121 exclusion in the deferred-sale option (he remains an owner; you have exclusive possession and indemnify the mortgage; sale or refinance triggered on a fixed date — e.g., 2032 or your youngest finishing middle school).
94: - **Corrected maintenance clause** (see §6) and **income-trust/notice language** so his February bonus installment ($22,500) is reported.
95: - If any IRA is divided later, no QDRO is needed (transfer incident to divorce, §408(d)(6), per `library/qdro_72t.md`).
96: 
97: ## 6. Maintenance: his own clause is legally wrong — a free win for you
98: 
99: His proposal says $2,000/month for 36 months, *"deductible to Husband and taxable to Wife."* For decrees **executed after Dec 31, 2018**, alimony is **neither deductible by the payor nor taxable to the recipient** — *TCJA §11051 (P.L. 115-97)* (`library/irc_1041_121_71.md`). Practical effect:
100: 
101: - You keep **all $72,000** (36 × $2,000) at the federal level. Under his mislabeled clause you would have owed ≈ **$17,280** (36 × $24,000 × 24%) — delete that language.
102: - To him the $72,000 costs a full $72,000 (he keeps no ~$17,280 deduction). Expect him to try to cut the amount on that basis; that trade is his to argue, not a reason for you to accept the bad wording.
103: - Child support is **never** deductible or includible (same file).
104: - For the **child-support worksheet only**, maintenance still shifts income: −$24,000 to him, +$24,000 to you (Columbia guidelines — see §7).
105: 
106: ## 7. Child support: his $1,830 figure is low — the right number is ≈ $2,023/month
107: 
108: The guidelines include **bonuses (expected/recurring, evidenced by employer documents)** in gross income (*Col. Rev. Stat. §14-10-115*; `library/columbia_child_support_guidelines.md`). His "bonus: none expected" affidavit is contradicted by his own HR letter (§8). Correct worksheet (see `child_support.json`):
109: 
110: 1. Gross: Husband $168,000 + $45,000 bonus = **$213,000**; maintenance adjustment −$24,000 → **$189,000**. Wife $72,000 + $24,000 → **$96,000**.
111: 2. Net (× 0.78 ÷ 12): H **$12,285**, W **$6,240** → combined **$18,525**.
112: 3. Two children, ≤ $20,000 bracket → basic obligation **$3,050**.
113: 4. Husband's share = $3,050 × (12,285 ÷ 18,525) = **$2,022.63/month** (his proposal's salary-only math gives $1,830 — **$192.63/month ≈ $2,312/year short**). Bonus sensitivity — you confirmed he "always gets a bonus" and 2025 was ~$40,000: a $40,000 bonus → gross $208,000, adj. $184,000, net $11,960, combined $18,200 → share **$2,004.29**; the $45,000 letter figure → **$2,022.63**; $50,400 at his 112% pace → **$2,041.74**. All three stay in the same $3,050 bracket, so the answer is robust: **≈ $2,004–$2,042/month** regardless of which bonus figure a court adopts.
114: 5. No shared-parenting discount: he has ~30% overnights, below the 35% threshold; you are the residential parent (≥ 65%).
115: 6. Support continues through the children's minority — the worksheet excerpt does not state termination terms **[unverified — unresolved, §10]**; with kids aged 12 and 9 that is roughly 6 and 9 years of stream, so correcting his income is worth ≈ **$14k–$21k** over time even before any retroactive award **[retroactivity rules not in library — unverified]**.
116: 
117: ## 8. The undisclosed bonus: what to do now
118: 
119: - **What it is:** sworn affidavit (2026-08-30): "Bonus: discretionary; none expected for 2026." Discovery (2026-09-22): HR letter (2026-03-02) promising a **$45,000 target bonus** (paid 50% September / 50% February) with him already at **112% of plan** (→ up to **$50,400**); and a pay stub showing YTD gross **$146,212** vs pro-rated salary **$119,000** — **$27,212 unexplained**, consistent with the ≥$22,500 September installment, with **~$4,712 still unexplained** even on that theory (source: unresolved — §10).
120: - **Now a pattern, not a one-off:** you (round-2 response) confirm he **"always gets a bonus"** and 2025 was **≈ $40,000** — his affidavit ("none expected") is false as to 2026 *and* inconsistent with a recurring multi-year pattern. That (a) independently satisfies the guideline test for including **expected or recurring bonuses** in gross income (*Col. Rev. Stat. §14-10-115*) even apart from the HR letter, and (b) strengthens the Rule 16.2 disclosure-violation narrative: this is a pattern of concealing the single largest variable in his pay, made under oath. Your history claim is **client-reported** — pin it to employer records (his 2024–2025 W-2s, 401(k) deferral statements, brokerage deposits) in discovery so it becomes evidence, not testimony vs. testimony.
121: - **Why it matters:** sworn full disclosure of **bonuses and expected compensation** is mandatory (*Col. R. Fam. P. 16.2*; `library/columbia_equitable_distribution.md`), and his failure exposes him to **reopening of the judgment, sanctions, and an unequal division in your favor (Rule 16.2(e))**. It also changes the child-support base from $168,000 to $213,000–$218,400.
122: - **Play:** put the HR letter and pay stubs on the record; do not sign any settlement before (a) support is recalculated at true income, (b) his 2024–2025 W-2s, returns and plan statements confirm the bonus history (~$40,000 in 2025), and (c) the February $22,500 installment is covered by an income-withholding/notice order. The Rule 16.2(e) leverage is your best argument for the after-tax equalization in §4 — use it, and consider asking for unequal division (not just 50/50-after-tax) given the misconduct.
123: 
124: ## 9. Dependents and filing status
125: 
126: - Status is fixed **December 31** (*IRC §7703(a)*): if the decree is final by 12/31/2026 you file **Head of Household** (*§2(b)*) — you must pay **more than half the cost of the home**; keep receipts (mortgage, taxes, insurance, utilities, repairs). **[We cannot yet prove the >half test — house running costs unresolved, §10.]**
127: - With ~70% overnights you are the **custodial parent and claim both children** (*IRC §152(e)*). His "alternating years" plan works **only if you sign Form 8332**, and a release moves **only the child tax credit** — **HOH status, EITC, and the dependent-care credit stay with you** regardless (`library/filing_status_dependents.md`).
128: - Recommendation: **refuse blanket releases; price them.** The CTC's dollar amount is not in this library **[unverified]**, so treat each release year as a negotiated item (e.g., $X per release against the cash equalization). Also beware: selling the house solo in a later year could push you near the $200k NIIT threshold **[rate/threshold per `library/tax_rates_assumed.md`]**.
129: 
130: ## 10. Unresolved unknowns (client has no further information — flagged, not assumed)
131: 
132: Per your round-2 response, the items we asked that you could not answer stay open. They are **flagged here rather than assumed away**; each one either gets resolved in discovery (opposing party/employer/county records) or stays an explicitly labeled assumption:
133: 
134: 1. **House running costs** (property tax, insurance, HOA, utilities, maintenance) — needed to prove the HOH "more than half the cost of the home" test (IRC §2(b)) and to fully price carrying the house. Get the county tax statement and insurance declarations.
135: 2. **Your marginal tax rate** — the library fixes only Husband's 24% convention; your rate matters for pricing your 401(k) share and any Form 8332 release. Get your last return.
136: 3. **Ages / 59½ status of both parties** — drives the value of the §72(t)(2)(C) QDRO penalty exception and how hard to discount the 401(k)s.
137: 4. **Decree timing (before/after 12/31/2026)** — flips 2026 filing status (IRC §7703(a)) and interacts with the §121 exclusion timing if a sale is scheduled.
138: 5. **Child-support termination terms** (age 18/19/HS graduation; support for a child still in high school) — not in our library excerpt; length of the ~$2,023/mo stream depends on it.
139: 6. **Whether Husband will cooperate with Option C** (stay on title/loan, indemnity package) — the single biggest open variable; if he refuses, Option B (sell now) becomes the plan, since solo keep is off the table (§3).
140: 7. **Source of the residual ~$4,712** of the $27,212 YTD excess on the 2026-09-15 stub — discovery item (commissions? bonus advance? other income?).
141: 8. **Kids' add-on expenses** (health-insurance premium allocation, work-related childcare) — our worksheet excerpt has no add-ons section; relevant to add-on support requests and the dependent-care credit retention.
142: 
143: ## 11. Bottom line
144: 
145: No — as proposed it is not fair: face-value "halves" are worth about **$45,952 more to Husband** after tax (range $13,952–$93,952), his maintenance clause misstates post-2018 federal law, his child-support number is **$192.63/month low** (right number ≈ $2,023/mo; robust at $2,004–$2,042 across the bonus range), and he has sworn against his own HR letter. Your round-2 answers sharpen the path: the bonus is recurring (~$40k in 2025 → the affidavit is false twice over), and you cannot refinance $400,000 on $72,000 income — so keeping the house alone is off the table. Counter with **Option C** (deferred joint sale + QDRO $200,000 + 50/50 liquid splits ≈ **$661,707 each after tax**), with **Option B (sell now)** as the fallback if he won't stay on title, corrected support (**$2,022.63/mo**), maintenance stripped of the tax clause, dependents kept unless paid for — and keep the disclosure violation on the table.

102: - To him the $72,000 costs a full $72,000 (he keeps no ~$17,280 deduction). Expect him to try to cut the amount on that basis; that trade is his to argue, not a reason for you to accept the bad wording.
103: - Child support is **never** deductible or includible (same file).
104: - For the **child-support worksheet only**, maintenance still shifts income: −$24,000 to him, +$24,000 to you (Columbia guidelines — see §7).

106: ## 7. Child support: his $1,830 figure is low — the right number is ≈ $2,023/month

108: The guidelines include **bonuses (expected/recurring, evidenced by employer documents)** in gross income (*Col. Rev. Stat. §14-10-115*; `library/columbia_child_support_guidelines.md`). 115: 6. ## What I checked

- **Authority:** re-read all six files in `workspace/library/` against every citation in the deliverables; anything the library doesn't support is now labeled as an assumption or flagged `[unverified]`.
- **Facts:** re-checked every figure against `workspace/documents/` (asset schedule, affidavit, HR letter, pay stub, client goals).
- **Arithmetic:** re-ran a 69-check script covering every number in the deliverables (after-tax values, mortgage amortization, §121 shelter, all four division options, the full child-support worksheet and bonus sensitivities).
- **Schemas:** both JSONs re-parsed and matched key-for-key to the CONTRACT.md required shapes.

## What I fixed

1. **`advice.md` §3 — numeric error.** Said "≈ $762,700 interest remains." That's actually the total of the remaining 288 payments (principal *and* interest); interest alone is ≈ **$362,700**. Corrected.
2. **`division.json` alternative B — garbled figure.** Said the $734,000 gain was "sheltered to 468,000." The shelter is the **two $250,000 §121 exclusions ($500,000)** → $234,000 taxable. The downstream taxes ($21,996 / $17,550 / $39,546) were already correct and unchanged.
3. **NIIT on Husband's brokerage gain — labeled.** The library's stated NIIT convention covers only *Wife's* house gain; applying 3.8% to his brokerage gain is a conservative extension of IRC §1411. Now explicitly labeled as an assumption in both `advice.md` §2 and `division.json`.
4. **QDRO language — matched to source.** §5 now mirrors `library/qdro_72t.md`: absent a QDRO, a distribution to the participant to pay the former spouse is taxable to the participant and, if under 59½, subject to the 10% additional tax. (My earlier "you get nothing taxed-to-you basis" phrasing was muddled — deleted.)
5. **§408(d)(6) — sourcing nuance disclosed.** That section appears in the *body* of `library/qdro_72t.md` but not in that file's INDEX citation line; flagged at the citation point.
6. **Head-of-household test — completed.** The library requires both a qualifying child living with you >half the year *and* paying >half the home's cost; §9 (and `division.json`) now state both, noting your ~70% overnights satisfy the first.
7. **§1 caveat.** "His slice doesn't shrink under Option C" holds at the 24% and 32% conventions but **not** at the 12% sensitivity (there his own proposal leaves him ahead) — noted, with the standing advice to pin his real bracket.

## What I checked and deliberately did *not* change

- **`child_support.json` "$2,311.58/yr"** — I had flagged this as a rounding error, but re-derivation showed it's **correct**: it's the unrounded difference ($2,022.6316 − $1,830.00) × 12 = 2,311.58. The 2,311.56 figure would come from multiplying the already-rounded monthly number. Fix withdrawn.
- The "≈ $14k–$21k" support stream and "≈ $63k–$70k" total stack: exact values are $13,870–$20,804 and $62,568–$69,503 — the "≈" phrasing is accurate.
- The $18,525 combined net, $3,050 bracket, $2,022.63 share, $661,707 build-up, $51,446 tax saving, and the YTD $27,212 / $4,712-residual discovery trail all re-verified exactly.

Bottom line: the substance of the advice is unchanged — after-tax the proposal is $613,008/$658,960 (gap $45,952), Option C remains the recommendation, and support is ≈ $2,023/month — but the audit removed two numerical misstatements and closed three authority-precision gaps before delivery.
